title: Entanglement-Inducing Quantum Markov Processes
abstract: We introduce a new model for a system of interacting bosons placed in an array of sites. At its core is a nonlinear, nonlocal evolution equation, which we have dubbed the Schrödinger-Dirichlet equation. The construction is closely related to the Bose-Hubbard model and to a specific type of generalized bosons. In contrast to conventional mean-field closures, the resulting nonlinear dynamics need not preserve product structure and can generate entanglement from initially separable states. The relevant methods of analysis are based on harmonic analysis for the multiplicative group of positive rationals.
summary: This paper introduces the Schrödinger-Dirichlet equation (SDE) to model interacting bosons, proposing a novel, non-dissipative quantum Markov process capable of generating entanglement. The mathematical analysis is highly technical, relying on harmonic analysis on the group of positive rationals and analyzing the evolution of quantum states in Fock space.
main_problem: The paper develops a mathematical framework to analyze nonlinear, nonlocal quantum dynamics for interacting bosons, specifically focusing on the generation of entanglement from initially separable states.
main_result: The proposed Schrödinger-Dirichlet equation (SDE) generates entanglement, and the analysis utilizes harmonic analysis on the multiplicative group of positive rationals to characterize the system's evolution.
method: The analysis combines quantum field theory techniques (Fock space, generalized bosons) with advanced mathematical tools, including harmonic analysis on $\mathbb{Q}^+$ and the study of nonlinear differential equations for probability distributions.
model_or_system: The core model is a system of interacting bosons on an array of sites, governed by the nonlinear Schrödinger-Dirichlet equation (SDE). The analysis is mathematically grounded in the structure of the bosonic Fock space and its representation via the group $\mathbb{Q}^+$.
key_observables: Entanglement generation, entropy $E(P)$, expectation values of local number operators $\langle \hat{N}_q angle$, and the functional $F = \|\psi \odot \psi\|^2$.
important_parameters: The structure of the interaction (nonlinear, nonlocal), the nature of the underlying group ($\mathbb{Q}^+$), and the time evolution parameter $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a generalized-bosonic creation operator and relies on harmonic analysis techniques applicable to the multiplicative group of positive rationals.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes refer to tables summarizing Critical Points (CPs) for two-particle states and figures illustrating the behavior of functionals $F_+$ and $F_-$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing classical Markov processes (discrete and continuous time) to introducing the quantum mechanical model for bosonic sites indexed by primes, culminating in the analysis of entanglement-inducing functionals.
why_interesting: The work bridges quantum many-body physics (interacting bosons) with advanced mathematical structures (harmonic analysis on $\mathbb{Q}^+$), providing a non-standard, non-dissipative framework for studying quantum dynamics and entanglement.
